description: The data collected may be resold to other 3rd parties
title: Available for resale

description: Data is available to 3rd parties not involved in the data activity. This does not always mean that data is being resold.
title: Available to 3rd parties

description: Data that can be accessed and downloaded online, either for free or for a fee
title: Available to download

description: Available to me but not to other individuals. For example, as an individual you have access to all your electronic toll records for your car, but other individuals do not have access to that.
title: Available to me

description: Data is available to the accountable organization
title: Available to the accountable organization

description: Data is available to the data collection or technology provider
title: Available to vendor

description: Not available to me or other individuals. As an individual, there isn't a way for you to access this data.
title: Not available to me

description: Data is not available to the accountable organization
title: Not available to the accountable organization

description: Data is not available to the data collection or technology provider.
title: Not available to vendor

description: The entity that is responsible and accountable for this data collection activity
title: Institution

description: The entity that is responsible and accountable for this data collection activity
title: Organization

description: Compressed data into a binary format.
title: Binary

description: Data that has one of two data values, for example true and false.
title: Boolean

description: Information about identifiable individuals.
title: Personal

description: A digital image is composed of a grid of individual pixels.
title: Pixel-based Image

description: Data that represents a location, such as an address, a place name or geographic coordinates; or a structure, such as a floorplan.
title: Spatial

description: Data that is stored in a table, where values are stored in rows and columns.
title: Tabular

description: Measurements that are collected at regular intervals over a period of time.
title: Values / Time

description: Data that has been grouped or summarized from individual measurements, for example to count up totals or to calculate an average.
title: Aggregated

description: Data that is processed by automated, algorithmic or artificial intelligence systems to derive a new result or data point.
title: AI System

description: Bitmap manipulation is the process of altering pixels in a raster-based image, such as retouching a digital photograph.
title: Bitmap manipulation

description: Code signing is the process of digitally signing executables and scripts to confirm the software author and guarantee that the code has not been altered or corrupted since it was signed. The process employs the use of a cryptographic hash to validate authenticity and integrity.
title: Code signing

description: Computer vision refers to computer science methodologies that enable computers to derive data from digital images or video.
title: Computer vision

description: Cryptonets are neural networks that can be applied to encrypted data. Due to this capability it is not required to decrypt the data during processing and because of this it is not necessary to even provide the application host with the keys to decrypt the data. Cryptonets are an implementation of Homomorphic Encryption.
title: Cryptonets

description: Data that is processed to remove identifying values, usually to protect privacy. De-identification can happen at any point in a data collection process, for example before it is stored in a database, or before it is published. Here we define it to mean after the data has already left a hardware device, or after it has been stored in a database.
title: De-identified

description: Differential privacy is a system for publicly sharing information about a dataset by describing the patterns of groups within the dataset while withholding information about individuals in the dataset.
title: Differential privacy

description: Data has been encoded so that only authorized parties can access it, which can reduce risk related to handling private or sensitive information.
title: Encrypted

description: Encryption at Rest is the encryption of data when it is persisted to a storage medium like a drive or database. It protects the data against unauthorized access of the database itself.
title: Encrypted at Rest

description: Federated Learning involves both Edge Computing and a Cloud based process which allows machine learning to take place on a large body of decentralized de-identified data.
title: Federated learning

description: 3rd Party auditing specialists periodically examine the hardware & firmware to identify security best practice vulnerabilities and/or gaps in disclosure when it comes to the type of data the device is capturing and how it is being processed.
title: Hardware audits

description: Homomorphic encryption is a form of encryption that allows computation on ciphertexts, generating an encrypted result which, when decrypted, matches the result of the operations as if they had been performed on the plaintext.
title: Homomorphic encryption

description: All interactions with the data throughout its lifecycle, including access and any transformations that are applied are registered in an immutable query ledger creating an auditable chain of accountability mediated by a distributed database.
title: Immutable Query Ledger

description: K-Anonymity is used to ensure anonymity when disclosing otherwise personally identifiable data. Attributes of the data are suppressed or generalized until each row is identical with at least k-1 other rows. At this point the database is said to be k-anonymous.
title: K-Anonymity

description: Data that has not been processed or altered from the point of collection - the data is effectively identical to how it was gathered from the original data source.
title: Raw data

description: Data activity has undergone a Responsible Data Use Assessment and determined to provide a net benefit. The RDUA is a process that Sidewalk Labs conducts prior to the start of any data activity.
title: RDUA Approved

description: Depending on the jurisdiction and type of data, data is regulated in various ways
title: Regulated

description: Many organizations have internal review processes that consider the potential benefits, risks and implications for privacy for new technologies or data collection activities.
title: Reviewed Internally

description: Secure multi-party computation is a subfield of cryptography with the goal of creating methods for parties to jointly compute a function over their inputs while keeping those inputs private. It allows participants to generate aggregated insights from data while keeping the individual items of data secret.
title: Secure Multi-Party Computing

description: Transport Layer Security, or TLS, is a widely adopted security protocol designed to facilitate privacy and data security for communications over the Internet by encrypting data while it is in.
title: Transport Layer Security

description: A TEE is an isolated environment created using  special purpose hardware and software to protect the data stored inside. A TEE provides a “trusted environment” inside which a process can run while it is invisible to any other process on the processor, the operating system or any other type of privileged access.
title: Trusted Execution Environment

description: A Zero Knowledge Proof is a method by which one party can prove to another party that they know a value, without conveying any additional information such as the value itself.
title: Zero Knowledge Proofs

description: Ensures that everyone has equal access to a space or a service.
title: Accessibility

description: Enables you to control or interact with aspects of a space or a technology.
title: Agency & Interaction

description: Enables artistic and/or cultural expression.
title: Arts & Culture

description: Enables the buying and selling of goods and services.
title: Commerce

description: Enables a user to connect to a network, such as the internet
title: Connectivity

description: For providing food or meal services.
title: Dining

description: Supports the measurement or monitoring of the natural environment.
title: Ecology

description: Reduces energy use and/or helps conserve energy.
title: Energy Efficiency

description: Used for enforcement of rules or regulations.
title: Enforcement

description: Supports authentication or validation in order to access a space or a service.
title: Entry

description: Supports services that ensure public safety and health related to emergencies.
title: Fire & Emergency

description: Supports the measurement or monitoring of the aspects of the physical environment that impacts human health, such as radiation or air quality, or in specific contexts such as the workplace.
title: Health

description: Supports the provision of information, for example about a location, a service, or to provide assistance
title: Inform

description: Supports the movements of goods or materials.
title: Logistics

description: Supports how people and materials move around.
title: Mobility

description: Supports the development of future plans; or to enable or measure the impact of a decision.
title: Planning & Decision-making

description: Supports exploratory research and testing.
title: Research & Development

description: Enables a safe and/or secure environment, for example for the purposes of fire safety, home security or ensuring safe passage in places such as airports or roads
title: Safety & Security

description: For interacting with another person or a group.
title: Social

description: Supports a mechanical function - such as turning a device on or off, opening or closing, or adjusting brightness and intensity.
title: Switch

description: Supports the handling and disposal of waste, including as recyclables, compost and hazardous materials.
title: Waste Management

description: Reduces water use and/or helps conserve water.
title: Water Efficiency

description: Enables navigation of a location and its amenities and services.
title: Wayfinding & Services

title: Retained 2 years

description: Data is backed up outside the jurisdiction where it was collected.
title: Backed up internationally

description: Data is backed up with the jurisdiction where it was collected.
title: Backed up locally

description: No data is kept or stored
title: No data retained

description: Data is stored for 1 month, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 1 month

description: Data is stored for 1 year, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 1 year

description: Data is stored for 24 hours, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 24 hours

description: D﻿ata is stored for 2 years, and then after that time period is deleted.
title: Retained 2 years

description: Data is stored for 3 months, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 3 months

description: Data is stored for 5 years, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 5 years

description: Data is stored for 6 months, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 6 months

description: Data is stored for 7 years, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 7 years

description: Data is retained indefinitely
title: Retained indefinitely

description: Data is stored for 6 years, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained 6 Years

description: Data is stored for two weeks, and after this time period is deleted
title: Retained two weeks

description: In a shared data store model the data store is shared across multiple parties and because the infrastructure is shared it becomes possible to enforce governance around the retention, access and destruction of the data by policies built into the structure of the data itself.
title: Shared storage and governance

description: Data is stored in the jurisdiction where it was collected.
title: Stored locally

description: Data is stored on behalf of the organization or the data collector in an off-site data centre, such as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure
title: Stored on 3rd Party Cloud

description: Data is stored outside the jurisdiction where it was collected.
title: Stored primarily internationally

description: Data is stored mainly in the jurisdiction where it was collected.
title: Stored primarily locally

description: Measures various aspects of air quality, such as pollen, particulate matter, ozone, and greenhouse gases.
title: Air Quality

description: Provides access to assistive services. Examples include assistive technologies and virtual assistants
title: Assistance Station

description: Augmented reality is a technology that combines both physical and digital content to create interactive experiences and content.
title: Augmented Reality

description: Biometrics are body measurements and calculations related to human characteristics.
title: Biometrics

description: This devices uses a cellular communication network where the last link is wireless, enabling portable transceivers (e.g., mobile phones) to communicate with each other and with fixed transceivers and telephones anywhere in the network.
title: Cellular

description: A chatbot is a computer program designed to simulate human conversation with users.
title: Chatbot

description: Contactless payment systems are are credit cards and debit cards, key fobs, smart cards, or other devices, including smartphones and other mobile devices, that use radio-frequency identification (RFID) or near field communication (NFC) for making secure payments.
title: Contactless Payments

description: Generates still images of a sufficient resolution where individuals can be identified, for example by capturing images of faces or unique numbers such as vehicle license plates. However, images are processed in a way that removes identifying characteristics before it is used or stored (known as *de-identified before first use* or *de-identified on device*), for example by blurring faces using computer vision.
title: De-identified Image

description: Generates video footage of a sufficient resolution where individuals can be identified, for example by capturing images of faces or unique numbers such as vehicle license plates. However, the video is processed in a way that removes identifying characteristics before it is used or stored (known as *de-identified before first use* or *de-identified on device*), for example by blurring faces using computer vision.
title: De-identified Video

description: Generates audio data that can identify individuals, but the data is processed in a way that removes identifying characteristics before it is used or stored (known as *de-identified before first use* or *de-identified on device*).
title: De-identified Voice

description: The DTPR API provides machine-readable access to a place-centric registry of systems and sensors that are described using the open-source DTPR taxonomy.
title: DTPR API

description: An electric vehicle charger (EV charger) supplies power for recharging plug-in electric vehicles.
title: Electric vehicle charger

description: Facial characterization allows a system to make inferences such as gender, facial expression, and age range, but does not identify individuals. The technology does not retain or use any personally identifiable information.
title: Facial characterization

description: GPS is one of the global navigation satellite systems that provides geolocation and time information to a GPS receiver anywhere on or near the Earth where there is an unobstructed line of sight to four or more GPS satellites.
title: GPS

description: Describes a technology where the primary mode of interaction does not require the use of hands, for example, devices that respond to voice commands or gesture based "touchless" interfaces.
title: Hands-free

description: Generates still images of a sufficient resolution where individuals can be identified, for example by capturing images of faces or unique numbers such as vehicle license plates. Identifying information can be collected either through manual review of images by a person, or through computer vision techniques that derives information in the form of data from images.
title: Identifiable Image

description: A wireless communication protocol for electronic devices that are within a short distance of each other, typically used in ticketing or payment systems. In this case, unique identification is possible, for example if a particular item is closely associated with an individual's personal data.
title: Identifiable NFC

description: Enables the identification of items using electromagnetic fields, commonly used to track inventory in stores. In this case, unique identification is possible, for example if a particular item is closely associated with an individual's personal data.
title: Identifiable RFID

description: Generates video footage of a sufficient resolution where individuals can be identified, for example by capturing images of faces or unique numbers such as vehicle license plates. Identifying information can be collected either through manual review by a person, or through computer vision techniques that derives information in the form of data from video or images.
title: Identifiable Video

description: W﻿iFi sensors measure the strength of the wireless signals from cell phones and other mobile devices.  These measurements can be used to track the positions and movement of these devices in physical space. This may be associated with the hardware addresses of the devices themselves.
title: Identifiable WiFi Sensor

description: Generates still images.
title: Image

description: Generates still images in the infrared portion of the electromagnetic spectrum.
title: Image - infrared

description: Measures the slope, angle or tilt of objects based on gravity.
title: Inclinometer

description: An induction loop uses a moving magnet to generate an electric current in a nearby wire. When a metal object moves close to the wire it changes the current. This makes it useful for detecting vehicles or other metal objects.
title: Induction Loop

description: An intercom (intercommunication device) is a stand-alone voice communications system for use within a building or small collection of buildings, and is separate from other communications networks (such as the telephone system).
title: Intercom

description: Uses lasers to measure distances to objects, collecting data that can create a 3-D representation of the object.
title: LiDAR

description: Beacons are Bluetooth low energy (LE) hardware transmitters  that broadcast their identifier to nearby portable electronic devices. The technology enables smartphones, tablets and other devices to perform actions when in close proximity to a beacon.
title: Location Beacon

description: A device that generates audio.
title: Microphone

description: A sensor that detects the movement of nearby objects.
title: Motion Detector

description: A wireless communication protocol for electronic devices that are within a short distance of each other, typically used in ticketing or payment systems. No identifying data is collected in this case.
title: NFC

description: Generates video footage incapable of identifying individuals due to factors such as low-resolution, so that faces or unique numbers such as vehicle license plates cannot be determined.
title: Non-identifiable Video

description: An electronic sensor that measures infrared (IR) light radiating from objects in its field of view.
title: Passive Infrared Sensor

description: Person detection refers to when a system can detect the presence of humans in images or videos, and identify where they are located or how many there are in an image, but does not identify individuals. The technology does not retain or use any personally identifiable information.
title: Person detection

description: A mobile device that combines cellular and mobile computing functions into one unit, that is intended for use by one person.
title: Personal Device

description: Measures changes in pressure, acceleration, temperature, strain, or force by converting them to an electrical charge.
title: Piezoelectric sensor

description: Uses radio waves to detect objects, or measure how they are moving through a space, such as vehicles.
title: Radar

description: Enables the identification of items using electromagnetic fields, commonly used to track inventory in stores, but not for identifying individual items.
title: RFID

description: Soil moisture sensors measures the water content in soil.
title: Soil Moisture Sensor

description: Takes acoustic measurements, most typically for measuring noise pollution.
title: Sound Level Meter

description: People can interact with this digital system using the screen that is provided as part of device installation.
title: System Screen

description: Supports a mechanical function - such as turning a device on or off, opening or closing, or adjusting brightness and intensity.
title: Switch

description: Measures the temperature of or changes of temperature in the physical environment, and quantifies those attributes according to a standardized scale such as Celsius or Fahrenheit.
title: Thermometer

description: Uses ultrasonic waves to measure distances to objects. The sensor emits an ultrasonic wave and receives the wave reflected back from the object. The distance is calculated using the time between emission and reception.
title: Ultrasonic Sensor

description: An unmanned aircraft system (UAS) consists of an unmanned aircraft and the equipment necessary for the safe and effective operation of that aircraft. An unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is one component of this system.
title: Unmanned Aircraft System

description: Generates video footage.
title: Video camera

description: Generates video footage in the infrared portion of the electromagnetic spectrum.
title: Video camera - infrared

description: Audio data is collected that does or can identify individuals, either through manual review or by technologies that can determine either what is being said, or who is saying it.
title: Voice

description: Measures various aspects of water quality, such as the amount of dissolved oxygen in water, pH, nitrates and dissolved oxygen.
title: Water Quality

description: A set of instruments for measuring atmospheric conditions such as temperature, precipitation, wind speed and direction, and barometric pressure.
title: Weather Station

description: A weighing scale is a device to measure weight or mass. No identifying data is collected in this case.
title: Weighing Scale

description: Provides wireless access to a wired computer network, or to the internet.
title: Wireless Access Point

description: Copper coil segments buried under the road are activated to charge an electric vehicle battery using magnetic induction, which means that electric vehicles equipped with a special receiver can be charged while it is driving along or is parked over the road.
title: Wireless Charging Roadway
